NASB.2: 'Truly then you are the people, And with you wisdom will die!
NASB.3: 'But I have intelligence as well as you; I am not inferior to you. And who does not know such things as these?
NASB.4: 'I am a joke to my friends, The one who called on God and He answered him; The just [and] blameless [man] is a joke.
NASB.5: 'He who is at ease holds calamity in contempt, As prepared for those whose feet slip.
NASB.6: 'The tents of the destroyers prosper, And those who provoke God are secure, Whom God brings into their power.
NASB.7: 'But now ask the beasts, and let them teach you; And the birds of the heavens, and let them tell you.
NASB.8: 'Or speak to the earth, and let it teach you; And let the fish of the sea declare to you.
NASB.9: 'Who among all these does not know That the hand of the LORD has done this,
NASB.10: In whose hand is the life of every living thing, And the breath of all mankind?
NASB.11: 'Does not the ear test words, As the palate tastes its food?
NASB.12: 'Wisdom is with aged men, [With] long life is understanding.
NASB.13: 'With Him are wisdom and might; To Him belong counsel and understanding.
NASB.14: 'Behold, He tears down, and it cannot be rebuilt; He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
NASB.15: 'Behold, He restrains the waters, and they dry up; And He sends them out, and they inundate the earth.
NASB.16: 'With Him are strength and sound wisdom, The misled and the misleader belong to Him.
NASB.17: 'He makes counselors walk barefoot And makes fools of judges.
NASB.18: 'He loosens the bond of kings And binds their loins with a girdle.
NASB.19: 'He makes priests walk barefoot And overthrows the secure ones.
NASB.20: 'He deprives the trusted ones of speech And takes away the discernment of the elders.
NASB.21: 'He pours contempt on nobles And loosens the belt of the strong.
NASB.22: 'He reveals mysteries from the darkness And brings the deep darkness into light.
NASB.23: 'He makes the nations great, then destroys them; He enlarges the nations, then leads them away.
NASB.24: 'He deprives of intelligence the chiefs of the earth's people And makes them wander in a pathless waste.
NASB.25: 'They grope in darkness with no light, And He makes them stagger like a drunken man.

ESV.5: In the thought of one who is at ease there is contempt for misfortune; it is ready for those whose feet slip.
ESV.6: The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God are secure, who bring their god in their hand.

ESV.10: In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of all mankind.
ESV.11: Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
ESV.12: Wisdom is with the aged, and understanding in length of days.
ESV.13: “With God  are wisdom and might; he has counsel and understanding.

ESV.15: If he withholds the waters, they dry up; if he sends them out, they overwhelm the land.
ESV.16: With him are strength and sound wisdom; the deceived and the deceiver are his.

ESV.18: He looses the bonds of kings and binds a waistcloth on their hips.
ESV.19: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the mighty.

ESV.21: He pours contempt on princes and loosens the belt of the strong.
ESV.22: He uncovers the deeps out of darkness and brings deep darkness to light.
ESV.23: He makes nations great, and he destroys them; he enlarges nations, and leads them away.
ESV.24: He takes away understanding from the chiefs of the people of the earth and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
ESV.25: They grope in the dark without light, and he makes them stagger like a drunken man.

NKJV.5: A lamp is despised in the thought of one who is at ease; It is made ready for those whose feet slip.
NKJV.6: The tents of robbers prosper, And those who provoke God are secure— In what God provides by His hand.
NKJV.7: “But now ask the beasts, and they will teach you; And the birds of the air, and they will tell you;
NKJV.8: Or speak to the earth, and it will teach you; And the fish of the sea will explain to you.

NKJV.14: If He breaks a thing down, it cannot be rebuilt; If He imprisons a man, there can be no release.

NLT.2:
“You people really know everything, don’t you?
And when you die, wisdom will die with you!
NLT.3:
Well, I know a few things myself —
and you’re no better than I am.
Who doesn’t know these things you’ve been saying?
NLT.4:
Yet my friends laugh at me,
for I call on God and expect an answer.
I am a just and blameless man,
yet they laugh at me.
NLT.5:
People who are at ease mock those in trouble.
They give a push to people who are stumbling.
NLT.6:
But robbers are left in peace,
and those who provoke God live in safety —
though God keeps them in his power.
NLT.7:
“Just ask the animals, and they will teach you.
Ask the birds of the sky, and they will tell you.
NLT.8:
Speak to the earth, and it will instruct you.
Let the fish in the sea speak to you.
NLT.9:
For they all know
that my disaster has come from the hand of the LORD.
NLT.10:
For the life of every living thing is in his hand,
and the breath of every human being.
NLT.11:
The ear tests the words it hears
just as the mouth distinguishes between foods.
NLT.12:
Wisdom belongs to the aged,
and understanding to the old.
NLT.13:
“But true wisdom and power are found in God;
counsel and understanding are his.
NLT.14:
What he destroys cannot be rebuilt.
When he puts someone in prison, there is no escape.
NLT.15:
If he holds back the rain, the earth becomes a desert.
If he releases the waters, they flood the earth.
NLT.16:
Yes, strength and wisdom are his;
deceivers and deceived are both in his power.
NLT.17:
He leads counselors away, stripped of good judgment;
wise judges become fools.
NLT.18:
He removes the royal robe of kings.
They are led away with ropes around their waist.
NLT.19:
He leads priests away, stripped of status;
he overthrows those with long years in power.
NLT.20:
He silences the trusted adviser
and removes the insight of the elders.
NLT.21:
He pours disgrace upon princes
and disarms the strong.
NLT.22:
“He uncovers mysteries hidden in darkness;
he brings light to the deepest gloom.
NLT.23:
He builds up nations, and he destroys them.
He expands nations, and he abandons them.
NLT.24:
He strips kings of understanding
and leaves them wandering in a pathless wasteland.
NLT.25:
They grope in the darkness without a light.
He makes them stagger like drunkards.

AMP.2:
"No doubt you are the [only wise] people [in the world],
And wisdom will die with you!
AMP.3:
"But I have intelligence and understanding as well as you;
I am not inferior to you.
Who does not know such things as these [of God's wisdom and might]?
AMP.4:
"I am a joke to my friends;
I, one whom God answered when he called upon Him—
A just and blameless man is a joke [and laughed to scorn].
AMP.5:
"He who is at ease has contempt for misfortune,
But misfortune is ready [and anxiously waiting] for those whose feet slip.
AMP.6:
"The tents of the destroyers prosper;
And those who provoke God are [apparently] secure,
Whom God brings into their power.
AMP.7:
"Now ask the animals, and let them teach you [that God does not deal with His creatures according to their character];
And ask the birds of the air, and let them tell you;
AMP.8:
Or speak to the earth [with its many forms of life], and it will teach you;
And let the fish of the sea declare [this truth] to you.
AMP.9:
"Who among all these does not recognize [in all these things that good and evil are randomly scattered throughout nature and human life]
That the hand of the LORD has done this,
AMP.10:
In whose hand is the life of every living thing,
And the breath of all mankind?
AMP.11:
"Does the ear not put words to the test,
Just as the palate tastes its food [distinguishing between the desirable and the undesirable]?
AMP.12:
"With the aged [you say] is wisdom,
And with long life is understanding.
AMP.13:
"But [only] with Him are [perfect] wisdom and might;
He [alone] has [true] counsel and understanding.
AMP.14:
"Behold, He tears down, and it cannot be rebuilt;
He imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
AMP.15:
"Behold, He restrains the waters, and they dry up;
Again, He sends the waters out, and they overwhelm and devastate the earth.
AMP.16:
"With Him are might and sound wisdom,
The misled and the misleader are His [and in His power].
AMP.17:
"He makes [great and scheming] counselors walk barefoot
And makes fools of judges.
AMP.18:
"He loosens the bond of kings
And binds their loins with a loincloth.
AMP.19:
"He makes priests walk barefoot,
And He overturns men firmly seated and secure.
AMP.20:
"He deprives the trusted ones of speech
And takes away the discernment and discretion of the aged.
AMP.21:
"He pours contempt on princes and nobles
And loosens the belt of the strong [disabling them].
AMP.22:
"He uncovers mysteries [that are difficult to grasp and understand] out of the darkness
And brings black gloom and the shadow of death into light.
AMP.23:
"He makes nations great, and He destroys them;
He enlarges nations, and leads them away [captive].
AMP.24:
"He removes intelligence and understanding from the leaders of the people of the earth
And makes them wander and move blindly in a pathless waste.
AMP.25:
"They grope in darkness without light,
And He makes them stagger like a drunken man."

and when you die there'll be no one left to tell us how to live.

But don't forget that I also have a brain—
I don't intend to play second fiddle to you.
It doesn't take an expert to know these things.
MSG.4:
"I'm ridiculed by my friends:
'So that's the man who had conversations with God!'
Ridiculed without mercy:
'Look at the man who never did wrong!'
MSG.5:
It's easy for the well-to-do to point their fingers in blame,
for the well-fixed to pour scorn on the strugglers.
MSG.6:
Crooks reside safely in high-security houses,
insolent blasphemers live in luxury;
they've bought and paid for a god who'll protect them.
MSG.7:
"But ask the animals what they think—let them teach you;
let the birds tell you what's going on.
MSG.8:
Put your ear to the earth—learn the basics.
Listen—the fish in the ocean will tell you their stories.
MSG.9:
Isn't it clear that they all know and agree
that God is sovereign, that he holds all things in his hand—
MSG.10:
Every living soul, yes,
every breathing creature?
MSG.11:
Isn't this all just common sense,
as common as the sense of taste?
MSG.12:
Do you think the elderly have a corner on wisdom,
that you have to grow old before you understand life?
MSG.13:
"True wisdom and real power belong to God;
from him we learn how to live,
and also what to live for.
MSG.14:
If he tears something down, it's down for good;
if he locks people up, they're locked up for good.
MSG.15:
If he holds back the rain, there's a drought;
if he lets it loose, there's a flood.
MSG.16:
Strength and success belong to God;
both deceived and deceiver must answer to him.
MSG.17:
He strips experts of their vaunted credentials,
exposes judges as witless fools.
MSG.18:
He divests kings of their royal garments,
then ties a rag around their waists.
MSG.19:
He strips priests of their robes,
and fires high officials from their jobs.
MSG.20:
He forces trusted sages to keep silence,
deprives elders of their good sense and wisdom.
MSG.21:
He dumps contempt on famous people,
disarms the strong and mighty.
MSG.22:
He shines a spotlight into caves of darkness,
hauls deepest darkness into the noonday sun.
MSG.23:
He makes nations rise and then fall,
builds up some and abandons others.
MSG.24:
He robs world leaders of their reason,
and sends them off into no man's land.
MSG.25:
They grope in the dark without a clue,
lurching and staggering like drunks.

NRSVCE.2:
“No doubt you are the people,
and wisdom will die with you.
NRSVCE.3:
But I have understanding as well as you;
I am not inferior to you.
Who does not know such things as these?
NRSVCE.4:
I am a laughingstock to my friends;
I, who called upon God and he answered me,
a just and blameless man, I am a laughingstock.
NRSVCE.5:
Those at ease have contempt for misfortune,
but it is ready for those whose feet are unstable.
NRSVCE.6:
The tents of robbers are at peace,
and those who provoke God are secure,
who bring their god in their hands.
NRSVCE.7:
“But ask the animals, and they will teach you;
the birds of the air, and they will tell you;
NRSVCE.8:
ask the plants of the earth, and they will teach you;
and the fish of the sea will declare to you.
NRSVCE.9:
Who among all these does not know
that the hand of the LORD has done this?
NRSVCE.10:
In his hand is the life of every living thing
and the breath of every human being.
NRSVCE.11:
Does not the ear test words
as the palate tastes food?
NRSVCE.12:
Is wisdom with the aged,
and understanding in length of days?
NRSVCE.13:
“With God are wisdom and strength;
he has counsel and understanding.
NRSVCE.14:
If he tears down, no one can rebuild;
if he shuts someone in, no one can open up.
NRSVCE.15:
If he withholds the waters, they dry up;
if he sends them out, they overwhelm the land.
NRSVCE.16:
With him are strength and wisdom;
the deceived and the deceiver are his.
NRSVCE.17:
He leads counselors away stripped,
and makes fools of judges.
NRSVCE.18:
He looses the sash of kings,
and binds a waistcloth on their loins.
NRSVCE.19:
He leads priests away stripped,
and overthrows the mighty.
NRSVCE.20:
He deprives of speech those who are trusted,
and takes away the discernment of the elders.
NRSVCE.21:
He pours contempt on princes,
and looses the belt of the strong.
NRSVCE.22:
He uncovers the deeps out of darkness,
and brings deep darkness to light.
NRSVCE.23:
He makes nations great, then destroys them;
he enlarges nations, then leads them away.
NRSVCE.24:
He strips understanding from the leaders of the earth,
and makes them wander in a pathless waste.
NRSVCE.25:
They grope in the dark without light;
he makes them stagger like a drunkard.

NET.2: “Without a doubt you are the people, and wisdom will die with you.
NET.3: I also have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
NET.4: I am a laughingstock to my friends, I, who called on God and whom he answered — a righteous and blameless man is a laughingstock!
NET.5: For calamity, there is derision (according to the ideas of the fortunate ) — a fate for those whose feet slip!
NET.6: But the tents of robbers are peaceful, and those who provoke God are confident — who carry their god in their hands.
NET.7: “But now, ask the animals and they will teach you, or the birds of the sky and they will tell you.
NET.8: Or speak to the earth and it will teach you, or let the fish of the sea declare to you.
NET.9: Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this,
NET.10: in whose hand is the life of every creature and the breath of all the human race.
NET.11: Does not the ear test words, as the tongue tastes food?
NET.12: Is not wisdom found among the aged? Does not long life bring understanding?
NET.13: “With God are wisdom and power; counsel and understanding are his.
NET.14: If he tears down, it cannot be rebuilt; if he imprisons a person, there is no escape.
NET.15: If he holds back the waters, then they dry up; if he releases them, they destroy the land.
NET.16: With him are strength and prudence; both the one who goes astray and the one who misleads are his.
NET.17: He leads counselors away stripped and makes judges into fools.
NET.18: He loosens the bonds of kings and binds a loincloth around their waist.
NET.19: He leads priests away stripped and overthrows the potentates.
NET.20: He deprives the trusted advisers of speech and takes away the discernment of elders.
NET.21: He pours contempt on noblemen and disarms the powerful.
NET.22: He reveals the deep things of darkness, and brings deep shadows into the light.
NET.23: He makes nations great, and destroys them; he extends the boundaries of nations and disperses them.
NET.24: He deprives the leaders of the earth of their understanding; he makes them wander in a trackless desert waste.
NET.25: They grope about in darkness without light; he makes them stagger like drunkards.
